title: Truthful Bandit Mechanisms for Repeated Two-stage Ad Auctions

problem.claim: Design an online learning policy for first-stage subset selection in repeated two-stage ad auctions while satisfying game-theoretic requirements.

gap.claim: Truthful bandit mechanisms face a linear regret lower bound, creating a challenge for simultaneously achieving allocation efficiency and truthfulness.

contributions.claim: The work models the setting as a combinatorial bandit mechanism with a general reward function, truthfulness, and individual rationality.
It introduces truthful alpha-approximation oracles and evaluates mechanisms using alpha-approximation regret.
It proposes an explore-then-commit mechanism and a second mechanism with improved distribution-dependent regret under additional assumptions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an O(T) regret lower bound for truthful bandit mechanisms.
The first proposed mechanism is ex-post truthful and ex-post individually rational, with regret O(T2/3).
The second mechanism is reported to achieve O(log T /ΔΦ2) regret, where ΔΦ is a distribution-dependent gap.

narrative_sequence.summary: Two-stage ad auctions first select promising candidates and then run an auction using second-stage click-through-rate predictions.
The work studies online learning for first-stage subset selection subject to truthfulness and individual rationality.
A linear regret lower bound demonstrates the difficulty of jointly achieving allocation efficiency and truthfulness.
Truthful alpha-approximation oracles are introduced to work around the impossibility result.
Two ex-post truthful and ex-post individually rational mechanisms are proposed, with different regret guarantees and assumptions.

source_observation.claim: Truthfulness imposes a linear regret lower bound for the considered bandit mechanisms.

interpretation.claim: Strategic constraints can fundamentally limit achievable learning efficiency.

application.claim: When designing online mechanisms, analyze incentive constraints jointly with statistical regret rather than optimizing allocation efficiency alone.

exception.claim: The reported improved regret guarantee requires additional assumptions about the approximation oracles and strategic bidders.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal mechanism definitions or oracle constructions.
The abstract does not provide experimental settings, datasets, or independent verification of the reported guarantees.
